title: Who gets the information? An $\alpha$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
abstract: arXiv:2611.32200v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection disagree on how to distribute relevance over labels: some amplify features that inform a few labels, others balance what every label receives. We show these choices are implicit social welfare functions. Treating labels as agents whose utility is the information they receive, we propose FLIC, which greedily maximises the $\alpha$-fair welfare of per-label information coverage. A single parameter $\alpha$ moves from utilitarian ($\alpha=0$) through proportionally fair ($\alpha=1$) to max-min selection ($\alpha\to\infty$), and a dozen published relevance terms lie on this axis, most as special cases, first-order approximations or limits. The objective is monotone submodular for every $\alpha\ge0$ whenever each label's information is, so greedy selection is a $(1-1/e)$-approximation; this fails for $\alpha<0$, and the max-min limit is inapproximable. translated_title: 谁获得信息？一个用于多标签特征选择的 α-公平标签覆盖框架
translated_abstract: 近来的信息论多标签特征选择过滤器在如何将相关性分配到各标签上存在分歧：一些方法放大那些能为少数标签提供信息的特征，另一些则平衡每个标签所接收的信息。我们证明这些选择实际上是隐含的社会福利函数。我们将标签视为以所接收信息为效用的智能体，提出 FLIC，它贪婪地最大化每标签信息覆盖的 α-公平福利。单一参数 α 从功利主义（α=0）经过比例公平（α=1）过渡到最大最小选择（α→∞），十几种已发表的相关性度量都位于这条轴上，其中大多数是特殊情形、一阶近似或极限。当每个标签的信息是单调次模时，对于每个 α≥0 该目标函数也是单调次模的，因此贪婪选择可获得 (1-1/e) 近似保证；该性质在 α<0 时失效，且最大最小极限情形是不可近似的。（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 FLIC 框架，将多标签特征选择中不同的相关性分配策略统一解释为隐含的社会福利函数，通过单一公平参数 α 实现从功利主义到最大最小的信息覆盖分配，并证明在 α≥0 时贪婪选择具有 (1-1/e) 的近似保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes FLIC, a framework that unifies existing multi-label feature selection criteria as implicit social welfare functions over per-label information coverage, controlled by a single fairness parameter α ranging from utilitarian to max-min, and proves greedy selection achieves a (1-1/e)-approximation for α≥0.
